title: operational-priorities-hypothesis-canvas-v0-1
body:
Purpose and intended audience:
- Rapidly align leadership and cross-functional partners on 3 operational priorities to carry into Q4 and next planning cycle. Primary audience: execs + cross-functional leads. Secondary: team leads prepping all-hands talking points.

High-level framing (one line each):
1) Predictable cost-per-request: drive 20% unit-cost reduction on medium-latency workloads via batching, kv-cache, and quantization profiles.
2) Global reliability fabric: reduce P95 tail incidents impacting customer routes by 50% through routing improvements and rollout automation.
3) Developer time-to-value: shorten time to deploy a model with observability from 2 weeks -> 3 days via templates and onboarding flows.

Hypothesis canvas (for each priority):
PRIORITY A: Predictable cost-per-request- Hypothesis: If we provide model-specific batching & quantization recommendations in Optimize + automated autoscaling presets, customers will see >=20% token cost savings without measurable QoE regression.- Signal(s) to watch: median cost/token, 95th percentile latency for sampled prompts, revert rate in rollouts, customer feedback NPS on cost.- Leading metrics: number of models with 'optimize-recommendations-applied', percent of traffic routed to quantized variant, quantized inference error delta (LM score).- Risks & mitigations: quality regressions (mitigate with quick eval harness and canary), infra scheduling hotspots (mitigate with capacity cap and routing fallback), confusing UX (mitigate with copy + in-console simulation).- Required initiatives: Optimize rule-engine work, rollout dashboards, 2 canary customers for dedicated testing, update docs and SDK samples.- Owner(s): Eng-runtime (Diego), Product-optimize (Ava).- Quick experiment (3-week): roll out quantization profile for 1 popular open model on hosted-api for small percentage traffic -> monitor cost, latencies, and evaluation set quality.- Expected impact (90-day): 10% measured unit-cost improvement platform-wide if pilot successful; stretch to 20% with broader rollout.

PRIORITY B: Global reliability fabric- Hypothesis: If we add policy-aware routing + regional fallback + faster canary rollbacks then customer-visible outages from capacity loss will decline by half.- Signal(s): customer-route error-rate, mean time to recovery (MTTR) for degraded routes, number of cross-region fallbacks invoked.- Leading metrics: route-failure events/day, average fallback latency, automatic-fallback success ratio.- Risks & mitigations: cross-region data egress concerns (add explicit consent + doc), inadvertent performance regressions during routing change (staged canary).- Required initiatives: routing policy UI in Console, SRE-runbook updates, automated rollback triggers, test harness for region failover.- Owner(s): SRE (Lena), Platform-engineering (Diego).- Quick experiment (4-week): simulate region outage for internal traffic and verify fallback correctness and observability.- Expected impact: reduce customer visible route outages by 30–50% in 3 months; improves SLA compliance for Dedicated customers.

PRIORITY C: Developer time-to-value- Hypothesis: If we ship onboarding templates + 1-click model pinning + route templates in Console, teams will reduce time from sign-up to production by 60%.- Signal(s): average days between account creation and first production route, number of support tickets labeled 'onboarding friction'.- Leading metrics: template adoption rate, success rate of template-deployed routes, drop-off points in onboarding flow.- Risks & mitigations: templates don't fit edge cases (provide advanced template variants), scope creep (keep MVP narrow).- Required initiatives: Console templates, quickstart CLI commands, sample app updates, developer-facing runbook.- Owner(s): Developer-ex (Priya), Product-console (Ava).- Quick experiment (2-week): pilot template for embeddings workflow with three small partners; measure onboarding time and errors.- Expected impact: 40–60% reduction in TTV for targeted use cases in 60 days.

Cross-priority dependencies and sequencing:
- Batching/quantization work depends on serving-runtime kernel-selection improvements (eng-serving-runtime).
- Routing policy requires Console changes; coordinate with Product-console and release-engineering for staged rollout windows.
- Templates rely on smaller infra changes (deploy API that supports pinning and route blueprints).
- Need dedicated capacity for canary experiments — request 1 reserved GPU pool for four-week pilots.

All-hands / Exec update brief (condensed bullets for slide + speaker notes):
- Why this matters: Unit economics + reliability + developer TTV gate our ability to scale adoption into enterprise accounts. Small % improvements compound on our usage-led revenue model.
- What we will measure: concrete targets (20% unit-cost reduction target; 50% P95-incident reduction; 60% TTV reduction for templates).
- Early signs of progress: initial canary for quantization (week 1), region-failover drill (week 3), template pilot (week 2).
- Key asks of execs: sign-off to reallocate two infra hires to serving-runtime for 8 weeks, approval for reserved canary capacity budget, and alignment on customer communication cadences for any visible regressions.

Draft run-of-show for demo in all-hands (10 minutes):
1) 60s context (CEO) — why ops priorities now.
2) 120s demo: console 'template' flow (Priya) — show 1-click deploy.
3) 120s demo: cost calc and Optimize recommendation (Ava) — before/after pilot.
4) 120s short SRE play: simulated region failover and fallback (Lena).
5) 60s ask and next steps (Ava).

Internal signals tracker (example items to instrument in parallel):
- product: template-adoption, onboarding funnel drop-off points.
- infra: quantized-variant-percentage, batch-size distribution, kernel selection churn.
- sres: fallback-invocations, route-error spike alert counts.

Open questions / undecided items (to resolve before final OKR draft):
- What is the acceptable QoE delta threshold for quantization (LM-score delta vs cost) to mark as success? (proposal: <= 2% LM degradation on evaluation set).
- Do we prefer a platform-wide default batching policy or per-customer policy? tradeoffs: complexity vs control.
- How to communicate early regressions externally without eroding trust? (suggestion: private opt-in pilots + clear rollback).
- Headcount ask: exact scope for the two infra hires vs contractors?

Next steps (owners + dates):
- Finalize metric definitions and dashboards (Ava + Diego) — due 2025-10-09.
- Reserve canary capacity and schedule internal failover drill (Lena) — due 2025-10-06.
- Prepare all-hands demo scripts and lightweight slides (Priya) — due 2025-10-01.
- Kickoff pilot for quantization on hosted-api (Eng-runtime) — start 2025-10-03.

Notes to self / rough points to include in updated slide deck:
- Quick visual: stacked bar showing cost before/after with traffic % on quantized variant.
- One-liner in exec summary linking cost-savings to predictable gross margin expansion.
- Two short customer quotes (from pilot partners) if available — better than numbers alone.
- Keep ask slide explicit: hiring + budget + enablement time window.

Informal comments (work-in-progress):
- Keep language for all-hands short — avoid engineering jargon around KV cache. Use "response caching" instead.
- Consider a lightweight public blog post after stable rollouts that explains batching and quantization benefits for customers (marketing + comms).
- Align with legal on any cross-region fallback messaging for customers in regulated industries.

End of canvas.

Revision log: v0-1 initial draft created 2025-09-22 by Ava Nguyen; v0-2 edits planned after metric definitions are reconciled.
